status: DRAFT v0.1: not yet reviewed, pretested or calibrated.
notes: The values layer: reported separately as 'the values behind your views'. Agree/disagree statements come only in reverse-keyed pairs with defined scale points (Rule 6), so agreement bias cancels. Tradeoffs name what each side gives up. Written fresh for this project; none are copied from published scales.

items.stem: "A fair society keeps the differences in wealth between people small."
items.scope: Use the meanings shown for each answer.
point_meanings: True in nearly every case I can think of
True in most cases, with some real exceptions
I can see it both ways about equally
False in most cases, with some real exceptions
False in nearly every case I can think of

items.stem: "A fair society lets people keep what they earn, even if some end up far richer than others."
items.scope: Use the meanings shown for each answer.
point_meanings: False in nearly every case I can think of
False in most cases, with some real exceptions
I can see it both ways about equally
True in most cases, with some real exceptions
True in nearly every case I can think of

items.stem: Which kind of society would you rather live in?
items.scope: Think about the society as a whole, not your own place in it.

sides.label: Needs guaranteed
sides.text: Everyone's basic needs are guaranteed, even if taxes are high and people have fewer choices.

sides.label: Freedom to choose
sides.text: People are free to choose and keep more of what they earn, even if some go without.

items.stem: When the two conflict, which should usually win?
items.scope: Think about businesses and organizations open to the public.

sides.label: Equal treatment
sides.text: Protecting people from being turned away unfairly, even if owners lose some freedom to choose whom they deal with.

sides.label: Freedom to choose
sides.text: Owners' freedom to choose whom they deal with, even if some people are turned away unfairly.

items.stem: When the two conflict, which matters more to you?
items.scope: Think about society in general.

sides.label: Individual freedom
sides.text: Protecting individual freedoms, even if it's harder to keep order.

sides.label: Public order
sides.text: Keeping public order and safety, even if some freedoms are limited.

items.stem: When someone believes a law is wrong, which comes closer to what they should do?
items.scope: Think about laws in general, not one law.

sides.label: Follow conscience
sides.text: Follow their conscience, even if that means breaking the law.

sides.label: Obey the law
sides.text: Obey the law while working to change it, even if that means doing something they think is wrong.

items.stem: Which is more important to teach children?
items.scope: Think about children in general, not only your own.

sides.label: Think for themselves
sides.text: To question rules and think for themselves, even if they're harder to manage.

sides.label: Respect authority
sides.text: To respect rules and authority, even if they question less.

items.stem: Which approach to raising children is closer to your view?
items.scope: Children of elementary school age.

sides.label: Room to express
sides.text: Let children express themselves freely, even if they sometimes behave badly.

sides.label: Discipline and manners
sides.text: Expect discipline and good manners, even if that means stricter parenting.

items.stem: When the US government makes decisions, which comes closer to your view?
items.scope: Decisions on trade, aid, immigration and the like.

sides.label: Everyone counts equally
sides.text: Weigh people in other countries about as much as Americans, even if Americans sometimes lose out.

sides.label: Americans' interests first
sides.text: Put Americans' interests first, even if people elsewhere are worse off.

items.stem: Which comes closer to how you see yourself?
items.scope: Your own sense of loyalty.

sides.label: Humanity first
sides.text: My strongest loyalty is to humanity as a whole, more than to any one country.

sides.label: My country first
sides.text: My strongest loyalty is to my country, more than to humanity as a whole.

items.stem: When sharing out something valuable, which is fairer?
items.scope: Think of things like pay, benefits or public help.

sides.label: By need
sides.text: Those who need it most get more, even if they contributed less.

sides.label: By contribution
sides.text: Those who contributed more get more, even if some with greater need get less.

items.stem: In the US today, what mostly decides who gets ahead?
items.scope: Think about people in general, not any one person.
options: A mix of background, luck and effort

items.stem: Which comes closest to your view of right and wrong?
items.scope: Basic moral questions, not matters of taste.
options: Right and wrong depend entirely on the culture and the situation
Mostly depend on the situation, with a few fixed rules
There are many fixed rules, but some depend on the situation
Right and wrong are the same for all people and all times

items.stem: When society is changing, what pace of change is usually best?
items.scope: Changes in customs, laws and institutions.
options: As little as possible; keep what works
